cohort: Women who had recently given birth in England (n = 5,250) and Queensland, Australia (n = 3,467)
finding: The higher rates of caesarean birth in Queensland are largely attributable to higher rates of caesarean for women with a previous caesarean, and for the main reason of having had a previous caesarean.
mod_finding: Women in Queensland with a history of caesarean were more likely to have had a pre-labour caesarean and more likely to have had an intrapartum caesarean, due only to a previous caesarean.
